title: The Quadratic Formula and Completing the Square
seo_title: Algebra 1 Quadratic Formula Worksheets: Discriminant, Exact Answers and Completing the Square (Free, Answer Key)
short_title: Quadratic formula and completing the square
standard_text: Solve quadratic equations in one variable. Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x − p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.
meta_desc: Free Algebra 1 quadratic formula worksheets (A-REI.B.4): the discriminant, solving with the quadratic formula (rational and exact radical answers), completing the square, vertex form and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_sub: Discriminant b² − 4ac: positive → two solutions, zero → one, negative → none.
body_html:
How it works

For ax2 + bx + c = 0, the quadratic formula is x = (−b ± √(b2 − 4ac)) ÷ 2a. It works for every quadratic.

The discriminant b2 − 4ac tells you how many real solutions there are: positive → two, zero → one, negative → none.

To complete the square for x2 + bx, add (b/2)2: x2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)2. This also gives vertex form.

Example

Solve x2 − 4x − 1 = 0.

a = 1, b = −4, c = −1. b2 − 4ac = 20.

x = (4 ± √20) ÷ 2 = (4 ± 2√5) ÷ 2.

Answer: x = 2 ± √5

Example

Solve x2 + 8x + 7 = 0 by completing the square.

x2 + 8x = −7.

Add 16: (x + 4)2 = 9.

x + 4 = ±3.

Answer: x = −1 or x = −7

Common mistakes

  • Using b instead of −b at the start of the formula.
  • Dividing only the square root by 2a. The whole numerator is divided.
  • Getting the sign of c wrong in b2 − 4ac.
  • Adding b/2 instead of (b/2)2 when completing the square.

faq.q: What does the discriminant tell you?
faq.a: The value of b² − 4ac. If it is positive there are two real solutions, if it is zero there is one, and if it is negative there are none.

faq.q: How do you complete the square?
faq.a: For x² + bx, add (b/2)² to make a perfect square: x² + bx + (b/2)² = (x + b/2)². Add the same amount to both sides of an equation.

faq.q: When should I use the quadratic formula instead of factoring?
faq.a: When the quadratic does not factor easily with integers, or when you need exact or decimal answers.

items.q: Solve x2 − 10x − 11 = 0 by completing the square.
items.e: Move −11: x2 − 10x = 11. Add 25 to both sides: (x − 5)2 = 36. Square root: x − 5 = ±6, so x = −1 or x = 11.

items.q: What number should be added to x2 − 12x to make a perfect square trinomial?
items.e: Take half of −12 and square it: (−6)2 = 36. Then x2 − 12x + 36 = (x − 6)2.

items.q: Write x2 + 12x + 3 in the form (x + p)2 + q.
items.e: Half of 12 is 6. (x + 6)2 = x2 + 12x + 36, so subtract 36 to balance: 3 − 36 = −33. (x + 6)2 − 33.
